steps.notes: Literal implementation of the given base case (-1)^l*sqrt(2l+1)*j_l(kr0) + sectorial/main recursions passes 3/3 officially (review/work/22/step_22.1.py); hand-check of test 1 matches target to 6 digits analytically.

Literal prompt base case with scipy's standard (Condon-Shortley) Y fails tests 1 and 3 (1/3). Base = sqrt(4pi/(2n+1))*conj(Y_n^nu) reproduces all 3 targets BIT-EXACTLY (incl. the -3.7496997163e-17 FP residual) and passes 3/3 officially (review/work/22/step_22.2.py). Conjugated-harmonics (e^{-im phi}) world also fails test 1.

Correct forward-derived implementation: 1/4 (tests 2,3,4 fail). Independent quadrature projection (two sphere radii, agree to 10 digits) proves targets 2,3 are the complex CONJUGATE of the physical value and target 4's 'exactly 0' is physically 0.2176725262i. A gold-replica with two specific bugs (inverse-direction contraction + l>=|m| pruning) passes 4/4 officially (review/work/22/step_22.3_goldreplica.py).

findings.evidence: Background states the base case 'T_n^{nu 0}(Q) = sqrt(4pi/(2n+1)) Y_n^{-nu}(theta', phi')' but never defines the spherical-harmonic phase convention. With scipy.special.sph_harm/sph_harm_y (the standard Condon-Shortley convention and the only SH implementation in required_dependencies 'import numpy as np\nimport scipy'), the literal formula yields values flipped by (-1)^nu: official steptest verdict 1/3 (test 1: got -0.5 vs target +0.5; test 3: got +3.7497e-17-0.6123724j vs target -3.7497e-17+0.6123724j). Replacing the base with sqrt(4pi/(2n+1))*conj(Y_n^{nu}(theta',phi')) reproduces ALL three frozen targets bit-for-bit, including the tiny FP residual -3.749699716304616e-17 = -0.6123724356957946*cos(pi/2) in test 3 -- this is the literal formula under Gumerov-Duraiswami's convention where Y_n^m carries (-1)^m (signed m) with P_n^{|m|}, which differs from scipy by (-1)^m for m<0. The conjugated-harmonics (e^{-im phi}) reading also fails test 1 (-0.5 vs +0.5). So exactly one unstated convention choice passes; the natural scipy reading fails 2/3 tests.
findings.suggested_fix: State the Y_n^m convention explicitly in the step background, e.g. 'Y_n^m = (-1)^m sqrt((2n+1)/(4pi) (n-|m|)!/(n+|m|)!) P_n^{|m|}(cos theta) e^{im phi} for all signed m (Gumerov & Duraiswami)', or equivalently rewrite the base case for the scipy convention as T_n^{nu 0} = sqrt(4pi/(2n+1)) * conj(Y_n^{nu}(theta',phi')).

findings.evidence: Targets of tests 2 and 3 are the complex conjugate of the correct value. Problem statement: 'psi(r-r0) = sum B'_n^m R_n^m(r)'. Independent quadrature projection of the translated field onto Y_n^m on spheres of radius a=1.3 and a=0.9 (review/work/22/probe_22.3_projection.py, radii agree to 10 digits, test-1 value matches its target to 10 digits validating the method) gives test 2: -0.1525447968+0.1525447968j vs target -0.15254479680485558-0.15254479680485558j; test 3: -0.1444775833+0.2889551666j vs target -0.14447758329891097-0.28895516659782194j. The targets are instead reproduced (np.allclose) by contracting B against the re-expansion formula's OUTPUT-side indices (l,s) -- i.e. pattern-matching the function args (n,m) to the formula's free indices, which computes the inverse translation -- rather than the correct contraction B'_l^s = sum_{n,m,nu} B_n^m T_l^{s nu}(Q) T_n^{nu m}(Q^{-1}) (R|R)_{ln}^{nu}. Official steptest: correct forward implementation fails tests 2,3 (review/work/22/step_22.3_correct.py, 1/4); backwards-contraction replica passes (review/work/22/step_22.3_goldreplica.py, 4/4 joint PASS). No single convention world rescues this: under the only convention consistent with 22.2's targets (m>=0 outputs identical to scipy), the physical answers are the unconjugated values.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate targets 1-3 from a reference that contracts B on the formula's (n,m) slots (forward translation): expected targets become the conjugates of the current test-2/3 values (test 1 unchanged, it is real). Alternatively, if the inverse-direction reading is intended, the prompt must state explicitly the formula for B'_n^m in terms of B.

findings.evidence: Test 4 asserts '(compute_BRnm(r0, B, n, m, wl, N_t) == 0) == target' with frozen target np.True_, i.e. the returned coefficient must be EXACTLY the float 0. Physically it is not zero: for r0=(0,0.5,0), B_1^1=1, n=2, m=2 the quadrature projection gives BR_2^2 = 0.2176725262j (two radii, |value| >> 1e-10), and every self-consistent recursion chain tried gives nonzero (+/-0.2177j or +/-0.00197j depending on convention; review/work/22/probe_22.3_chain.py grid). The exact 0 only appears when the l-sum is restricted to l >= |m| (the only B entry sits at l=1 < |m|=2, so the sum is empty): adding that pruning to the backwards-contraction replica reproduces ALL FOUR targets exactly and passes official joint scoring (probe_final.py section C, step_22.3_goldreplica.py). Nothing in the prompt or formula (sum_{l=|nu|}^infty) licenses l >= |m|. Independently, '== 0' exact float equality would be fragile even if zero were the right answer (any 1e-17 roundoff fails it).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace test 4 with a value test: assert np.allclose(compute_BRnm(...), target) where target is the correct complex value (-0.2176725262j for the forward-translation reading) regenerated from a fixed reference; never gate on exact '== 0' for a float recursion output.

findings.evidence: 22.3's sums need T at negative second order and (R|R) at negative nu, but the prior steps only define the non-negative path: 22.1's recursion is initiated from (R|R)_{l0}^0 raising m upward ('which can be used to initiate the recursion process for all (R|R)_{lm}^m'), and 22.2's recursion only produces T_{n+1}^{nu,m+1} from T_n^{.,m} starting at m=0; both steps' tests use m>=0 exclusively. The required extensions ((R|R)^{-m}=(R|R)^{m} for coaxial translation; a negative-m symmetry for T) are unstated, and the T symmetry is convention-dependent: the target-reproducing replica requires T_n^{nu,-m} = (-1)^{|m|+|nu|} conj(T_n^{-nu,m}) (the standard-convention identity) even though the gold's base case follows the other convention -- the plain conjugation identity consistent with the gold's own base fails tests 1-3 of 22.3 (probe_final.py section C rows 3-4: match123=[False,False,False]).
findings.suggested_fix: Add the negative-order relations to the backgrounds: state (R|R)_{ln}^{-m} = (R|R)_{ln}^{m} in 22.1, and give the m<0 symmetry for T_n^{nu m} explicitly in 22.2.

findings.evidence: Cross-references to earlier steps were stripped from the text, leaving dangling sentences: 22.3 prompt 'Write a code to calculate the reexpansion coeffcient with and .'; 22.3 background 'The rotation matrix Q with the definition in can be generated by...'; 22.2 background 'the coefficients a_n^m and b_n^m are consistent with those in .'. Also 22.1's displayed equation sums over s ('sum_{s=-l}^{l}') but the summand contains no s. Inferable from context, but sloppy.

overall_assessment: Step 22.1 is fair and passes with a literal reading. Step 22.2 is solvable only by guessing the source paper's (Gumerov-Duraiswami) spherical-harmonic phase convention: the printed base-case formula under the standard scipy convention fails 2/3 tests, while the conj(Y) base matches targets bit-for-bit. Step 22.3 is effectively unpassable for a correct solver: its frozen targets encode TWO reference-code bugs -- the contraction of B against the wrong side of the re-expansion formula (targets 2,3 are the complex conjugate of the physical values, proven by independent quadrature) and an unjustified l >= |m| pruning that makes test 4's 'exactly 0' assertion true while physics gives 0.218j. A model is scored correct on 22.3 only if it reproduces both bugs. Recommend pinning the Y convention in 22.2 and regenerating all 22.3 targets from a corrected reference (replacing test 4's exact '==0' gate with an allclose value test).
